title: Sparse matrix models and kernel costs

items.title: Compressed sparse row matrices with stored-entry semantics
items.statement: Define the zero-based CSR arrays for an m by n matrix, including repeated columns, explicit zeros, empty rows, and the represented matrix; s counts stored entries and equals nnz only in the canonical case.
items.strategy: Specify the dimensions and array invariants, then define each matrix entry by the finite sum of stored values at that coordinate.

items.title: Structural graphs and ordered symmetric elimination
items.statement: Define the simple undirected nonzero-pattern graph of a real symmetric matrix, its graph update under a fixed elimination ordering, fill edges, and the later-neighbor parent forest.
items.strategy: Define the initial support graph and the finite neighbor-clique update at each ordered pivot; define each parent as the earliest later neighbor.

items.title: Validated compressed sparse row matrix-vector product
items.statement: Validate candidate CSR dimensions, row pointers, and column indices; return an explicit invalid-dimension or invalid-index status, or accumulate every stored entry once to return Ax in exact arithmetic.
items.strategy: Check dimensions first, validate the finite index arrays, initialize the output to zero, and perform one multiply-add per stored entry.

items.title: The filled graph contains every Schur-complement nonzero
items.statement: For an ordered real symmetric matrix with nonzero elimination pivots, every off-diagonal nonzero in each successive Schur complement is an edge of the corresponding filled graph; the later neighbors of each eliminated vertex form a clique.
items.strategy: Induct on the Schur-complement update: a nonzero updated entry either survives from the prior entry or comes from two nonzero pivot couplings, whose endpoints are joined by the graph update.

items.title: Validated CSR matrix-vector multiplication terminates with a status
items.statement: For finite candidate arrays and a finite vector, the validated CSR matrix-vector algorithm terminates, returning either its specified invalid-input status or an output vector.
items.strategy: Every validation loop has a finite array bound, and on valid input the row intervals partition the finite set of stored-entry indices.

items.title: CSR matrix-vector multiplication returns the represented product
items.statement: For every valid CSR record and vector x, the algorithm returns the represented matrix A times x in exact field arithmetic.
items.strategy: Prove the row accumulator equals the finite sum over its stored entries, then reindex the matrix-product sum by the unique stored column of each entry.

items.title: CSR storage and exact matrix-vector operation counts
items.statement: The CSR input uses exactly s value slots, s column-index slots, and m+1 row-pointer slots; on valid input the algorithm uses exactly s field multiplications, s field additions, and m zero initializations, with O(m+s) total storage and work for m at least one.
items.strategy: Count the three arrays and telescope the disjoint row-pointer intervals to count the stored-entry loop iterations.

title: Sparse matrix models and kernel costs — Examples

items.title: A four-row tridiagonal matrix in CSR form
items.statement: The 4 by 4 matrix with diagonal 2 and adjacent off-diagonal entries -1 has the displayed zero-based CSR representation with ten stored entries.
items.strategy: Check the row-pointer partition and column bounds, then expand each row's stored values into the represented matrix.

items.title: Eliminating the middle vertex creates structural fill
items.statement: Eliminating the middle vertex first in the three-vertex path matrix creates the edge between its two later neighbors and a nonzero Schur-complement entry there.
items.strategy: List the initial path graph, apply the neighbor-clique update, and calculate the first and remaining Schur pivots exactly.

items.title: Numerical cancellation can remove an entry from the structural pattern
items.statement: For a specified symmetric 3 by 3 matrix and ordering, the first Schur update cancels an existing off-diagonal value to zero while the filled graph retains that structural edge.
items.strategy: Compute the first Schur-complement entry and all pivots, then compare its numerical support with the graph update.

items.title: An exact CSR product and its stored-entry count
items.statement: For the four-row tridiagonal CSR matrix and x=(1,2,3,4), the product is (0,0,0,5), with ten multiplications, ten additions, four zero initializations, and 25 input storage slots.
items.strategy: Evaluate each row from its stored entries and count operations and array slots directly.

items.title: Duplicate columns and explicit zeros count as stored entries
items.statement: A 2 by 3 CSR record with duplicate column entries that cancel and one explicit zero represents the zero matrix while still having three stored entries.
items.strategy: Verify the row-pointer and column data, sum duplicate entries, and count all stored entries in the operation and storage formulas.
